description: MetLife is one of the world’s largest financial services companies, providing insurance, annuities, employee benefits and asset management to help individual and institutional customers build a more confident future.  Founded in 1868, MetLife has operations in more than 40 markets globally and holds positions in the United States, Asia, Latin America, Europe and the Middle East.

title: MetLife

rankings.title: 100 Best Large Workplaces for Women
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

"The culture here is unmatched by any other company I have worked for in the past. MetLife's team has genuinely valued my international background. The team has embraced the unique perspective, experiences, and ideas that come from my background. Rather than viewing my differences as something to overcome, MetLife has recognized them as strengths that contribute to innovation, collaboration, and better outcomes. This has allowed me to bring my whole authentic self to work every day."

rankings.title: Best Large Workplaces in Financial Services and Insurance
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say: 

"MetLife truly cares about your overall well-being. I've been with the company for 15 years, and when I had a health scare last year, management sprang into action and with my grateful agreement, put me into a role within the same department that gave me more flexibility to truly focus on healing. Giving time off work for doctor appointments and physical healing is fairly commonplace in corporate settings. Meeting as a management team to collectively and proactively move an employee into a new position, without it being a step down, that they knew would aid in mental healing as well is exceptional."

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
In 2021, MetLife introduced a floating cultural heritage holiday to give employees the flexibility to choose when and how to celebrate their own ethnicity. In 2022, the firm debuted an associated calendar, Moments That Matter, enabling staff to highlight key cultural events, learn about colleagues’ backgrounds, and find opportunities for allyship. The company also introduced custom skin tones and the option to add personalized pronouns and name pronunciation for staff participating in the myMetLife online community.
 

MetLife’s digitally enabled AI learning platform, MyLearning, allows employees to select specific skills they want to develop or use keywords to find already available content that will help them meet their goals. Boasting more than 300,000 assets to date, the platform was used by 73% of staff in 2023.
 

MetLife’s annual Employee Benefit Trends Study yields data the firm has used to demonstrate that a focus on the holistic well-being of workers yields higher levels of productivity, job satisfaction, loyalty, and engagement. Fueled by this research, MetLife aims to create a caring culture throughout the organization.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
The global financial services company is implementing innovative employee engagement programs to help achieve its diversity, inclusion, and impact goals.

  • MetLife has committed to investing $2.5 billion in DEI initiatives by 2030. In 2022, the company joined The Hispanic Promise, hosted the Triangle Tech X Conference aimed at lowering barriers for women in STEM, and issued a grant to Syracuse University’s Lender Center for Social Justice to research the origins of the racial wealth gap.

  • One of its DEI initiatives includes the Global DEI Leadership Council, which holds teams across the international company accountable to DEI goals.

  • MetLife’s internal MyPath platform helps employees connect with managers outside of their teams to grow into new roles while contributing to important work.

  • In 2023, MetLife is adding cancer support, digestive health support, family building support, and expanded mental health support for employees on the company health plan.

Everyone is open and honest but, also provides you with valuable feedback."

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
MetLife, the largest life insurance provider in the U.S., reported lower revenue and profit in 2022, as the company's finances were a victim of the year’s economic uncertainty. The company brought in $69.9 billion in revenue (down 1.7%) and $2.5 billion in profit (down 61.3%).

  • High inflation rates and fears of a recession contributed to the profit loss by driving down the returns of MetLife's investment portfolio, particularly in Q4 of 2022.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: MetLife is the largest life insurance provider in the U.S. and serves 100 million customers in nearly 50 countries. MetLife’s revenues for 2021 were up almost 5% over 2020, to $71.1 billion, and profits rose 21.2%, as strong gains in the insurer’s investment portfolio helped offset the impact of high payouts for deaths related to COVID-19. In 2022, MetLife announced diversity, equity, and inclusion commitments that include spending $5 billion with diverse suppliers by 2030 and committing $150 million in funding through the MetLife Foundation to support underserved and underrepresented communities over that same time span.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Like many insurers, MetLife felt the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on a financial level. Claims and payouts for life insurance policyholders rose as millions around the world died from COVID-19; a decrease in claims related to dental, property, and auto insurance, with customers stuck at home, wasn’t enough to counter the financial impact of those tragedies. Overall, revenues fell 2.6% to $67.8 billion, while profits dropped 8.3% from 2019. But if any business takes the long view, it’s insurance; in fact, at 153 years old, MetLife is one of the rare companies functioning today that also weathered the 1918 flu pandemic. CEO Michel Khalaf now says, “The worst impact of the pandemic on our business performance is behind us.”

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: In his first year on the job, MetLife CEO Michel Khalaf led the 156-year-old insurer through a relatively stable period with few major natural disasters to dent its balance sheet. With revenue up just 2.5% year-over-year, the nearly $70 billion-in-revenue company dropped seven spots on the Global 500. The insurer doesn’t expect the pandemic to have a significant impact on its financials this year; according to its forecasts, the modest addition of COVID-19-related accident and health claims will be counteracted by a decrease in dental and auto claims.
